drivingQuestion: What did Hannah mean by asking for 'zera anashim', an offspring of men?
outcomeNote: four aggadic readings stand side by side; the sugya decides between none of them, and Rav Dimi only elaborates the last

segments.en: Later in her prayer, Hannah says: «“And You will grant Your servant an offspring of men.”»

segments.he: מַאי ״זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים״? אָמַר רַב: גַּבְרָא בְּגוּבְרִין. וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: זֶרַע שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁחַ שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים, וּמַאן אִינּוּן — שָׁאוּל וְדָוִד. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: זֶרַע שֶׁשָּׁקוּל כִּשְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים, וּמַאן אִינּוּן — מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן בְּכֹהֲנָיו וּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּקוֹרְאֵי שְׁמוֹ״. וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: ״זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים״ — זֶרַע שֶׁמּוּבְלָע בֵּין אֲנָשִׁים.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is» the meaning of «“an offspring of men”? Rav said:» Hannah prayed for «a man among men,» a son who would be outstanding and exceptional. «And Shmuel said:» This expression means «an offspring who will anoint two men» to royalty. «And who were they? Saul and David. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» Hannah prayed that she would bear «an offspring who» would be «the equivalent of two» of the world’s greatest «men. And who were they? Moses and Aaron. As it is stated: “Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those who call His name”» (Psalms 99:6). In this verse, Hannah’s son, Samuel, is equated to Moses and Aaron. «And the Rabbis say: “An offspring of men”:» Hannah prayed for «an offspring who would be inconspicuous among men,» that he would not stand out in any way.

segments.he: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר לֹא אָרוֹךְ וְלֹא גּוּץ, וְלֹא קָטָן וְלֹא אַלָּם, וְלֹא צָחוֹר וְלֹא גִּיחוֹר, וְלֹא חָכָם וְלֹא טִפֵּשׁ.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «When Rav Dimi came» from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia, «he said» in explanation: Hannah prayed that her son would not be conspicuous among men; «neither too tall nor too short; neither too small nor too fat; neither too white nor too red; neither too smart nor too stupid.»
